title: Pay yourself first
text: Move a fixed amount into savings the day your allowance or part-time pay arrives, before any other spending happens.

title: Track every coffee
text: Small daily buys add up quickly. Writing down each coffee, snack or short ride for one month shows exactly where your money leaks.

title: Use the 50-30-20 starter split
text: A simple beginner guideline: 50 percent of income for needs, 30 percent for wants and 20 percent for savings. Adjust the shares to fit your situation.

title: Cover needs before wants
text: Plan rent, food, transport and study costs first. Optional spending should only get whatever is left after the essentials are covered.

title: Automate a small saver amount
text: Even a tiny amount moved to savings every week builds the habit. Consistency matters more than the size of the deposit.

title: Make savings goals specific
text: A goal like Rs 5,000 for a laptop in six months is easier to stick to than just save more. Name the target, amount and deadline.

title: Do a weekly money check-in
text: Spend ten minutes each week reviewing what came in and what went out. Small corrections early prevent a stressful end of the month.

title: Cancel what you never use
text: Unused subscriptions quietly drain a student budget. Review streaming, apps and memberships every few months and cut the dead weight.

title: Build a tiny emergency buffer
text: Save a small cushion, even one week of expenses, before chasing bigger goals. One surprise should not break your whole budget.

title: Wait 48 hours on wants
text: When something feels urgent, give it two days. If you still want it and your wants budget allows it, buy it guilt-free. If not, you just saved money.

title: Give every category a cap
text: Set a limit for food, transport and fun at the start of the month. When a cap is reached, that category waits until next month.

title: Celebrate small goal wins
text: When you hit a milestone, mark it with a free or low-cost reward. Positive feedback makes saving feel worthwhile instead of painful.
